# Summary of Cairn Rules

## Pulses

A pulse causes a cairn to grow. The new height equals the current height plus the stride plus a bonus. The bonus is calculated by counting how many complete stride-sized chunks fit into the current height. This creates acceleration—taller cairns grow faster because they have larger bonuses.

## Leaks

After a pulse, a leak removes marks equal to how many complete leak-sized chunks fit into the new height. Unlike pulses, leaks are based on a fixed leak size that stays the same each cycle. The amount lost changes because it depends on height, but the leak size itself never changes. Leaks act as a balancing mechanism to prevent unbounded growth.

## Drains

A drain is a fixed loss every cycle—the same number of marks are lost regardless of height. This is different from leaks, which scale with height. Drains can eventually cause cairns to stop growing or decline if they're large enough relative to pulse gains.

## Repeated Cycles

When performing multiple pulses, leaks, or drains in sequence, you must calculate each cycle individually. Each cycle depends on where the previous cycle ended because height affects bonus calculations.

## Finding Origins

To find what starting height produces a target result, you test candidates by running them forward through all the cycles and checking if you reach the target. There's no reverse formula—you only work forward.

## Merging

Two cairns combine using weighted contributions. Each cairn's height is multiplied by its weight (which must sum to 1). Each result is floored separately before combining. The floored values are added together to produce the merged height.
